subject: Post-call recap + proposed eval plan for MedLytics long-context use case
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@medlytics.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed eval plan for MedLytics long-context use case

Thanks again for taking the time today, Hannah — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short technical evaluation: 

Summary of needs we heard (from today's discovery):
- Primary workload: multi-page EHR notes (50–5,000 tokens), full-encounter summarization and structured extraction for downstream analytics.
- Key constraints: high summarization fidelity (no hallucinations on medications/diagnoses), deterministic truncation behavior (must never drop last 2 sections), and HIPAA-compliant handling of PHI.
- Success criteria: recall of critical entities >= 95% on our rubric; summaries <= 250 tokens and medically consistent; 99th percentile latency target for 2k-token requests < 1.2s on dedicated infra.

Proposed short evaluation (what Redwood can run with you):
1) Sanity check: run our long-context inference profile on a 200-record sample you provide (redwood runtime with KV cache enabled).
2) Model matrix: run the sample across two recommended variants: a) redwood-long-13b-q4 (higher-quality long window) and b) redwood-7b-long (faster, cost-efficient).
3) Prompt/pipeline: we’ll use an extraction-first prompt set (attached prompt_sets_v1.csv) plus a downstream summarization pass to evaluate hallucination/regression.
4) Metrics + artifacts: per-case token accounting, truncation flags, entity-level precision/recall, and example failure cases (we’ll share benchmark_preview_MedLytics.pdf).

Immediate asks from you to get started:
- Share a 200-record de-identified sample (or a signed DPA/processing agreement) and confirm preferred delivery method (Drive link or SFTP).
- Confirm timeline: is next-week pilot run okay (we can start processing Wednesday 5/13)?

I’ve looped in Rishi and Camila for model/ops specifics — Rishi will detail the recommended runtime/config and Camila will coordinate onboarding/procurement touches.

Attachments: prompt_sets_v1.csv (prompt templates + eval rubric), benchmark_preview_MedLytics.pdf (sample outputs).

Thanks — Neha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Post-call recap + proposed eval plan for MedLytics long-context use case

Nice recap, Neha. A few technical notes I want captured in the thread so we can agree before sending to MedLytics: 

Model recommendations (short):
- redwood-long-13b-q4: best for longest-context fidelity; supports 32k token windows (practical up to ~20k for contiguous attention), Q4 quantization balances memory and quality. Good default for recall-sensitive summarization.
- redwood-7b-long: good latency/cost sweet spot for batched throughput; opt for q4_0 with KV cache for repeated prefixes.

Truncation behavior and fidelity testing:
- We’ll instrument a truncation flag in the runtime that reports whether any document exceeded the model’s working window and where cutpoints occurred. That helps correlate fidelity drops with truncation events.
- For summarization fidelity, we’ll run targeted prompt-sets that force the model to list entities and cross-check against ground truth. The prompt set attached includes explicit "do not hallucinate" anchors.

Benchmark links + harness:
- Small public preview (internal): https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/long-context/2026/medlytics-preview
- Eval harness: internal repo + instructions are in the Drive folder we’ll share with the Data Science contact.

Config suggestions for pilot run:
- Use continuous KV caching enabled; batch size 8 for the 7b variant, 4 for 13b to avoid OOM in dedicated staging.
- Logging: token-level cost, latency P50/P95/P99, truncation boolean, entity recall/precision per case.

Attachments to include when we forward to the customer: prompt_sets_v1.csv, benchmark_preview_MedLytics.pdf, short readme on config knobs.

I can draft the exact model/config blurb — Neha, if you want, I’ll drop a suggested paragraph below for your outbound.

—Rishi

--- draft to customer ---
Hi Hannah — following our call, here are the concrete model/config recommendations we propose for the pilot: 
1) Primary: redwood-long-13b-q4 (32k capable) — run for fidelity-sensitive sampling.
2) Secondary: redwood-7b-long (q4_0) — use for batched throughput runs and cost comparisons.
Runtime/config: KV cache enabled; truncation flags on; batch=4 (13b) / 8 (7b).
What we need from you: 200-record JSONL sample (encounter_id, raw_text, redaction_level) and confirmation that we can begin processing 5/13.

Deliverables: per-case metrics (entity recall/precision), truncated-case flags, summary examples, and a short report with recommended rollout settings.

--- end draft ---

If that looks good I’ll send to Hannah and cc procurement. Camila — can you attach the SOW template (SOW_template_redwood.docx) and procurement contact items?

Thanks — Neha
